summary: Bundled the Unity web extension's CSS into the standalone `.web.js` output by emitting a style-install bootstrap, then updated Button, ConfirmDialog, SelectField, and console.css to use proper design tokens and components instead of inline/unstyled markup, and verified the rebuilt extensions/unity.web.js installs its CSS at runtime.
decisions: scripts/build-web-extension.ts now prepends a runtime CSS-install snippet that creates a <style data-gizmo-extension-style="unity"> tag and injects the collected CSS into document.head when the extension loads in the webview.
Replaced the native <select> in SelectField.svelte with the bits-ui Select primitive using Check + ChevronDown icons and a data-ui="select-indicator".
Replaced the inline confirmation UI in ConfirmDialog.svelte with the bits-ui Dialog primitive plus the local Button component, using onConfirm/onCancel callbacks and a void confirm() flow.

Refactored console.css to use semantic tokens (--space-*, --color-surface-soft, --text-2xs, --font-mono, --color-border, --radius-sm) and added a [data-ui="sr-only"] utility for screen-reader-only labels.
errors: Initial smoke test for the bundled CSS failed with 'console CSS missing' because the inline `node -e` check searched for the literal selector `[data-ui="console-toolbar"]` while the bundled output contained an unquoted attribute selector form; rewriting the assertion to look for `[data-ui=console-toolbar]` passed and the bundle was confirmed to install its CSS.
